H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper describes a flat repeated wait/open/wait/close PLC flow; no parent modes, nested states, or composite state structure are specified.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Transitions depend on low-level and high-level float switch signals X0/X1 and threshold-style sensor checks; the paper also states actions occur when both higher and lower sensors are triggered.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: The controller drives concrete outputs Y0/Y1 for gate opening/closing through relays, motors, and lead-screw actuation, but actions are mostly direct actuator commands.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: No implemented emergency stop, fault transition, rollback, or recovery path is defined for the sample; alarm discussion is generic PLC background.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: The I/O mapping X0/X1/Y0/Y1/M0 is given in the ladder/I-O sections, the wait-open-wait-close sequence is in the flowchart text, and actuator realization appears later in hardware implementation.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: M0 is described as an HMI control that operates gates regardless of water level, implying manual-override priority without fully spelling out the override transition rules.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions are narrated as prose: wait for sensor, open the gate, wait for second sensor, close the gate; attribution to Y0/Y1 relay and motor effects must be inferred across prose sections.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The paper states that if both the higher and lower sensors are triggered, the gate action occurs, giving a two-sensor boolean guard signal.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: There is no composite parent state with its own entry, during, or exit behavior.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: No from-any-state fault or recovery rule is declared.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain is present.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: There is at most a weak advantage from representing the two-float boolean guard over X0/X1; there are not three or more arithmetic/boolean guards.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: The HMI override applies regardless of water level, suggesting a cross-cutting manual control rule, but the paper does not enumerate enough substates for a strong N-to-1 forced-transition advantage.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: The main outputs are concrete PLC actuator commands Y0/Y1 to relays, motors, and gate mechanisms, not abstract log/publish/notify actions.

key_nl_quotes: The address X0 has been assigned to the low-level sensor of the dam, and the address X1 has been assigned to the high-level sensor of the dam.
Fig 5 explains that the process starts by getting signal from level sensor... opening the gate... wait for second sensor signal... close the gate and this process run repeatedly.
one_line_pitch: A compact PLC dam-shutter loop that stresses baselines through split I/O-to-flow mapping, manual override semantics, and guard/action attribution rather than hierarchy.
rationale: The sample has usable EFSM content with meaningful sensor guards and actuator outputs, but it is flat and lacks a real fault-recovery model. Its main stress value comes from baseline-trap density: the paper splits I/O mapping, behavioral flow, manual override, and actuator effects across sections. This makes it a good backup stress test for guard/action attribution, not a top candidate for hierarchical or recovery-heavy modeling.
